# 0003. Use payment webhooks with an hourly reconciliation poll

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-11-27
- **Supersedes:** [0002. Poll the payment provider for status](0002-poll-payment-status.md)

## Context

[0002](0002-poll-payment-status.md) chose polling because the provider offered no webhooks in April 2026, and said to revisit when it did. Facts from the [discussion on 2026-11-18](../../notes/webhooks-discussion.md) (Ana, payments; Ben, platform; Chloe, support):

- The provider launched signed webhooks on 2026-11-01. Each event carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the body, and events can arrive more than once.
- Polling costs 1.9 million provider calls a month. From 2027-01-01 the provider will charge for status calls over 1 million a month.
- Support reports that customers see paid orders as pending for up to 30 seconds.

## Options considered

- **Keep polling every 30 seconds.** No new endpoint to run. Keeps the delay of up to 30 seconds, and at 1.9 million calls a month it goes over the 1 million free calls once charging starts on 2027-01-01.
- **Switch to webhooks only.** Removes the status-call volume. Needs a public HTTPS endpoint, signature checks, and idempotent handling. Any event that never arrives leaves an order in the wrong status, with nothing to catch it.
- **Webhooks plus an hourly reconciliation poll.** Needs the same endpoint, signature checks, and idempotent handling as webhooks only, plus a poll that runs once an hour to catch missed events.

## Decision

Take payment status updates from the provider's webhooks, and run a reconciliation poll once an hour to catch missed events:

- Receive events on a public HTTPS endpoint.
- Reject any event whose HMAC-SHA256 signature over the body does not verify.
- Handle events idempotently, so an event that arrives more than once changes the order only once.
- Stop the 30-second poll from 0002 and replace it with the hourly reconciliation poll.

## Consequences

- Easier: status updates no longer wait for the next 30-second poll, and provider status calls drop from the 1.9 million a month of polling.
- Harder: the webhook endpoint is a new public service to monitor and secure, and the handlers must stay idempotent because events repeat.
- Ruled out: running without a public endpoint, which 0002 relied on.
- 0002 stays Accepted while this record is Proposed. When this record is accepted, change 0002's status to `Superseded by 0003`.
# 0002. Poll the payment provider for status

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-04-11

## Context

The payment provider offered no webhooks in April 2026.

## Options considered

- Poll every 30 seconds.
- Ask customers to refresh.

## Decision

Poll the provider's status endpoint every 30 seconds for open orders.

## Consequences

Easier: no public endpoint. Harder: up to 30 seconds of delay, and 2,880 calls a day per open order. Revisit when the provider offers webhooks.
